title: unforgettable korean pork jjim
description: a fresh, pillowy, energizing korean dish featuring apple cider vinegar and coconut cream. this dish is gluten-free friendly and is best served as a ssam.

ingredients.name: apple cider vinegar
ingredients.notes: use a high-quality vinegar for the best flavor

ingredients.name: coconut cream
ingredients.notes: chill the can in the refrigerator before opening

ingredients.name: sesame oil
ingredients.notes: use a light hand when adding to avoid overpowering the dish

instructions: in a large bowl, whisk together pork shoulder, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and 1 teaspoon of salt until the meat is well coated.
cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
preheat the oven to 300 degrees fahrenheit.
remove the pork from the marinade and place it in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot with a lid.
add the coconut cream, sesame oil, and black pepper to the pot.
cover the pot and transfer it to the preheated oven.
bake for 2 hours, or until the meat is tender and easily shreds with a fork.
remove the pot from the oven and let it cool slightly.
using two forks, shred the pork into bite-sized pieces.
return the pot to the stovetop and add the gochujang. stir to combine.
cook for an additional 10 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened slightly.
serve the pork warm, garnished with chopped green onions and additional gochujang if desired.
serve with steamed rice or kimchi for a filling meal.
adjust the level of spiciness to your liking by adding more gochujang or red pepper flakes.
serve with toasted sesame seeds and chopped green onions for added crunch.
add a fried egg on top for a satisfying breakfast or brunch option.
serve with a side of pickled radishes for a tangy contrast to the rich pork.
